view: The print turns on three things. The first is whether 'at least $200m' for FY2026 survives. The second is how much cash was left at 30 September after the equity contributions to Yotta 2 and NeutraDC Batam. The third is any word on the US data centre, which was targeted to close at the end of November. The Q3 revenue headline matters less: the company set the $48-50m range itself in late August and it controls recognition. My own arithmetic shows the FY guide was strained on the day it was given: $78.4m (H1) plus $48-50m (Q3) plus $60-70m (Q4) is $186-198m, below $200m, so the guide needs a Q4 of about $72m, above the company's own top end. Since then, Indian trade press (2026-10-05) reports two slips. The Yotta 1 B200 build, promised for the end of August, had only its first of four phases done in late September, with the rest due by mid-October. The 20,736-GPU Yotta 2 B300 programme slipped from 30 September to tranches running October to December, and revenue is recognised only once equipment is accepted and billing. That makes a trimmed or hedged FY number more likely than the stale $200m. Gross margin was about 4.9% in H1, which implies a negative Q2 gross profit, and depreciation ahead of slipped billing points to another weak quarter. The October toxic note says cash was tight. Against that, the price has already taken a lot: the financing and the LOI doubts are in it, the stock trades below 1x the revenue guide, and short interest is high. The company is promotional and has a record of attaching good news to prints (the +14% open in Q3 2025). A reaffirmed guide, Yotta 1 billing, or a signed US deal could squeeze a washed-out name 15-25%. On balance I lean slightly down, not far enough to act.
unpriced: Possibly the guide arithmetic. Taken together, the FY 'at least $200m' and the Q4 $60-70m planning range cannot both hold, and the counterparty-side reports of slipped Yotta deliveries (2026-10-05) came after the guide was set. I could not show that consensus or the price holds a trim, because the FY consensus was unavailable. But the price fall can be tied to the financing and the sector, not to a guide cut, so a cut would be a new step. The weight is small because management may simply reaffirm.

recommendation.reason: The evidence leans down: an internally inconsistent FY guide, slipped Yotta deliveries reported after it was set, weak gross margin and a funding squeeze. But the stock has already fallen 52% since September, much of it in a sector rout. High short interest and a promotional management team with a record of headline-positive prints make a squeeze just as plausible. I cannot see the deciding line well enough to reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A reaffirmed FY2026 guide of at least $200m with Yotta 1 confirmed billing and the first B300 tranches accepted in Q4, or a signed definitive agreement and financing for the US data centre.

self_critique: Management set the Q3 range itself in late August, knowing the Yotta timeline, and has a record of meeting top-line guides (FY2025 about $101m against about $100m). A promotional CEO will probably reaffirm the 'at least $200m' and stack positives into the release: a US deal close, NeutraDC at 18MW, B300 tranches. A stock down 52% at 0.9x revenue, with 18% short interest and a retail following, can gap up 15-20% on that, as it did in Q3 2025. My negatives (financing, margins) are already in the price, and the guide arithmetic may be resolved by rounding rather than a cut. That case is strong enough to keep me close to 50.
